body:
APGI Course Access and Commercial Pricing Policy

Policy for course scope, learner access, commercial options, revenue allocation and development recovery

Document reference | APGI COMM PRICE 001  Version 1.2 Review draft  Prepared 17 November 2026

Status | For approval  Effective only after recorded approval and activation

Policy owner | APGI Training Platform

Review | Within 12 months of activation or sooner when commercial rules or platform costs materially change



This policy sets the commercial rules for courses offered through the APGI platform. It is designed to let a person or organisation begin marketing or selling eligible learning without an upfront platform charge, while ensuring that paid learner activity recovers platform, delivery and course-development costs. It does not activate a price, waive a learner payment, or create a recognised educational credit claim. Those decisions remain subject to the approved price schedule, course record and applicable learning-credit controls.

1 Purpose

The policy explains which course types may be offered, the ways in which learning may be bought, the combinations that are permitted, and the reason for each commercial rule. It also defines how the buyer invoice is built, how normal course revenue is shared, and how APGI recovers the cost of a course it develops before transferring ownership.

2 Core commercial principles

APGI may allow a course owner or prospective training business to join, brand and market eligible courses before the owner has made a sale. Platform participation is not itself a free learner enrolment.

Each learner enrolment must be paid for unless APGI has approved and recorded a time-bound promotion with a funding source and scope.

Course content, LMS platform recovery, and card-processing treatment are distinct components. Only course-content revenue is allocated among the entitled course owner, selling platform and APGI. The prescribed allocations total 100 percent of that course-content revenue.

A larger commitment may reduce the course-content price per learner, but it does not remove eligibility restrictions, learner credit limits, access periods, or the need to recover platform use.

Financial planning credits, course-creator credits and internal proposed educational credits are separate measures. None may be represented as a formal learner credit unless the applicable recognition requirements have been met.

3 Course scope options

Every course record must state its scope before it can be priced or offered. Scope controls who may see, buy and enrol in the course. It also provides the commercial rationale for the relative price and margin applied in the approved calculator.

Course scope | Who may access it | Commercial rationale

Public | Any eligible learner or platform sharer, subject to normal platform terms. | Public courses are intended to be widely available. They should be positioned competitively and normally carry the lowest margin of the three scopes because volume and reach are expected to support recovery.

Industry specific | Learners and organisations within the defined industry or other approved audience. | Industry courses address a narrower market and may require specialist content, language or administration. They may carry a higher margin than public courses while still benefiting from group volume.

Client specific | Only the named client and its authorised learners unless the course owner approves a wider release. | Client-specific courses are commonly commissioned or configured for a particular organisation. Restricted access, lower scale and client obligations justify the highest margin and tighter approval controls.



A public, industry-specific or client-specific label does not decide who owns the course. Ownership is recorded separately as an own or existing course, or a course developed by APGI. A course owner may decide whether an eligible course is shared more broadly, but cannot remove the restrictions recorded for a client-specific or industry-specific course without the required approval.

4 Purchase options

The platform offers four buying routes so that a self-funded learner, a small organisation and a larger organisation do not have to buy the same kind of access. Each route has a different commercial purpose and entitlement boundary.

Purchase option | What is bought | Who it suits | Rationale

Individual course | One named course for one self-funded learner for the selected access period and credit allowance. | A learner paying personally or an organisation buying a single place. | Removes an annual platform commitment for an individual learner. The learner pays for the selected course and the applicable platform recovery for that access period.

Named-course seat pack | A prepaid number of places in one named course. | An organisation that needs a defined group to complete one course once. | Provides a lower content price through a known group commitment without requiring a year of platform access or a broad catalogue entitlement.

Learning wallet | A prepaid, controlled learner credit allowance for eligible courses during the selected access period. | An organisation that needs flexibility across an approved course range. | Allows learning to be allocated where it is needed while preventing an unrestricted catalogue promise. Each selected course draws its recorded credit value from the learner allowance.

Platform access subscription | Prepaid active learner seats for a defined term, with course-credit and course-count limits. | An organisation that wants planned platform access across multiple eligible courses. | Creates a predictable per-active-learner platform-access model comparable with market subscription pricing, while retaining controls over course scope, credits and duration.



5 Permitted option combinations

The following matrix states the normal combinations. A permitted combination remains subject to the course record, buyer eligibility, agreed access period and the current approved price schedule. A restricted combination is not automatically available merely because the calculator can model it.

Course scope | Individual course | Named-course seat pack | Learning wallet | Platform access subscription

Public | Permitted for one named course. | Permitted for prepaid places in the selected course. | Permitted for eligible public courses within the wallet limit. | Permitted for eligible public courses within the subscription limits.

Industry specific | Permitted only for an eligible learner with the required industry access. | Permitted for an eligible organisation and the named course. | Permitted only for an eligible organisation and approved industry course set. | Permitted only for an eligible organisation and approved industry course set.

Client specific | Requires written client access authorisation before enrolment. | Permitted for the named client and authorised group. | Permitted only for the named client when the wallet is explicitly configured for those courses. | Permitted only for the named client when the subscription is explicitly configured for those courses.



The platform must not represent a wallet or platform-access subscription as unrestricted access to every course. A learner may enrol only in courses that are within the recorded scope, available to the buyer, and covered by the learner's remaining internal proposed credits and course-count allowance.

6 Learner volume and commitment bands

Seat count affects the commercial adjustment, not the fundamental scope rule. The calculator must allow an exact whole-number seat count between fixed commercial stops so a buyer can model 100, 1,000 or another actual cohort size without losing the relevant pricing band.

Use case | Normal seat treatment | Why the rule exists

Individual purchase | One learner. Public individual pricing may use the approved minimum paid-learner denominator when recovering shared platform cost. | A learner should not be required to buy a full organisation subscription. The calculation still needs a sustainable platform-cost assumption.

Organisation purchase | Minimum 10 seats for a named-course seat pack, learning wallet or platform access subscription, unless APGI approves an exception. | A paid group commitment creates enough predictability to support a lower content price and administration of the buying route.

Industry course | Commercial bands begin at 10 seats and progress through 50, 150, 500, 1,000 and then 1,000-seat increments or an approved enterprise quote. | The bands reflect increasing scale while protecting the higher value of specialist industry content.

Client-specific course | The normal client band is 10 to 50 seats. A cohort above 50 requires a client or enterprise quote unless the approved price schedule states otherwise. | Client-specific work is less likely to scale through a public catalogue and may carry client service, privacy or change-control obligations.



The current calculator may show commercial stops at 10, 50, 100, 150, 500, 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000 seats. These controls make the main decision points easy to select. They do not prevent the buyer from entering a valid number between the stops, and they do not replace the approved volume rules in the price schedule.

7 Buyer price and invoice structure

The buyer invoice is made up of separate components so that course economics remain understandable. The course-content charge is the amount used for the 100 percent course-owner, selling-platform and APGI allocation. LMS recovery and buyer-paid card processing are added as separate items and do not change the stated course-revenue percentage split.

Invoice component | Policy treatment | Reason

Course-content charge | Set from the recorded course credit value, approved price-per-credit or cost-plus setting, course scope, volume adjustment and minimum content-price floor. | Reflects the value and delivery economics of the course. This revenue is allocated among the entitled course owner, selling platform and APGI under section 8.

LMS platform recovery | Calculated from the approved shared platform-cost pool, the defined learner-cost population, selected learner count and access term. Apply the consistent-unit and shortfall controls in section 7 1. | Keeps platform use visible and prevents a low course price from silently absorbing the cost of access, hosting, administration and support.

Card processing | Added to the buyer invoice, absorbed by the seller, or absorbed by APGI according to the selected approved fee treatment. | Makes the fee bearer clear before sale and avoids misrepresenting payment processing as course revenue.

Tax and other regulated charges | Applied separately where required. The calculator and price schedule must state whether displayed amounts are before or after tax. | Prevents a planning estimate from being mistaken for a final tax invoice.



For course-credit-price mode, the calculator uses the approved course-credit rate and volume adjustment to determine the content price. For cost-plus mode, the calculator uses known delivery and support cost together with the target seller margin. The approved price schedule, not this policy, records the current rates, cost pools, minimums, card rates and margin settings.

7 1 Controlled course calculator

APGI administrators and authorised platform-user business owners may use the same approved course calculator. APGI controls the shared platform-cost assumptions, approved fee schedules, global minimums and policy allocation rules. Platform users may enter their own permitted course and selling assumptions and see their own results. Internal partner distribution records and another organisation's private costs remain restricted.

The existing platform-costing module supplies a dated, approved cost snapshot to the course calculator. The calculation must use consistent units for shared monthly cost, the learner population and access duration. New paid enrolments per month and concurrently active learner-months are different measures. The approved price schedule must identify the denominator used, any forecast or minimum-volume assumption, and the responsible funding source for a projected recovery shortfall. The same cost must not be included twice.

Measured delivery and support costs must be entered or sourced from an approved estimate. An amount reverse-calculated from a desired price or margin must remain labelled as an assumption; it must not silently become a known cost. The calculator must show each recipient's applicable share, direct costs and estimated profit. A shared-course reseller's 10 percent commission must not be described as an 80 percent payout.

Save the calculator version, policy version, cost snapshot, course editions, rates, assumptions and calculated amounts with the commercial offer. A planning result does not approve a course or activate a charge. The exact required commercial approvals and buyer or company acceptance must be recorded before an offer becomes available for sale. Earlier approved offers and completed transactions retain their original calculation basis.

8 Course revenue allocation and ownership

8 1 Own or existing course

The normal allocation depends on who owns the course and who makes the sale. Record the course owner and the selling platform as separate roles, even when one organisation fills both roles. Each recipient pays its own agreed direct delivery, support or selling costs from its allocated share. A target profit margin must be assessed against the share that the recipient actually receives.

Sale arrangement | Course revenue allocation | Control

Course owner sells its own course | 80 percent to the course owner as seller  20 percent to APGI | This is the normal owner sale. APGI receives its full course fee for platform use, marketplace exposure and commercial administration.

APGI owned course sold by a platform user | 80 percent to the selling platform user  20 percent to APGI | The full APGI course fee remains with APGI because APGI owns the course.

Another platform user sells a shared course | 80 percent to the course owner  10 percent to the selling platform user  10 percent to APGI | The course owner receives 80 percent for its course. The selling platform earns 10 percent commission for the sale through its platform. APGI receives 10 percent as its platform fee.



Where a platform user sells a course owned by another platform user, the course must use the price recorded by the course owner. A seller may not substitute a lower course-owner price or alter the recorded scope without the course owner's authority. The commercial record must identify the course owner, seller and APGI allocation before publication.

8 2 Course developed by APGI

When APGI develops a course for a future course owner, APGI owns the course until the agreed development cost has been recovered and the ownership-transfer conditions have been met. During recovery, APGI receives its normal 20 percent course fee plus the temporary development-recovery amount set in the approved calculator or contract. The current model allows recovery of up to 25 percent of course revenue per sale, but never more than the outstanding balance.

The future owner receives the normal 80 percent seller share less the applied recovery amount during that period. After the development balance reaches zero and APGI confirms the transfer, the course returns to the normal 80 percent future-owner and 20 percent APGI split. The recovery balance must be tracked separately from APGI's normal course fee so the owner can see what remains outstanding.

8 3 Internal platform distributions

APGI's internal cost reimbursements, development-funding repayment and partner profit distributions are governed by the separate approved internal agreement. External course-owner entitlements and selling commissions must be provided for before the relevant residual platform income is distributed. Collecting an amount through APGI does not make the entire buyer invoice distributable platform profit. An expense already recovered through LMS recovery, a course share or another approved reimbursement must not be recovered or deducted a second time.

When APGI sells an APGI-owned course directly, the course-owner and selling-platform roles belong to the same platform business. Consolidate those role amounts in that business's records before applying the separate internal cost and distribution rules. Do not invent an external seller payout.

9 Course creator access and earned development support

APGI may make the course-creator platform available to people who wish to start a training business before they can afford a conventional LMS or course-development service. Access to eligible public and industry courses for marketing and resale does not create a right to free learner enrolments, unrestricted course creation, or access to restricted client content.

A course owner may use the shared APGI hosting domain without a separate domain-hosting charge. A custom branded domain is optional and may carry the published monthly hosting charge, currently planned at USD 20 per month. Any change to that amount is a price-schedule change, not a policy amendment.

The first course-creation entitlement is earned, not an automatic sign-up gift. APGI may fund a first course after the platform user's realised sales have generated enough APGI course contribution to recover the estimated course-creation cost and the approved margin. The exact qualifying sales threshold must be calculated from verified cost and actual APGI contribution per sale, then displayed to the user before the entitlement is awarded.

Course creation may be bought through a market-related subscription, a pay-as-you-go credit top-up, or earned credits where the qualification rule is met. Before a user starts course generation, the platform should estimate the credits required, expected cost and whether available earned credits cover it. Automatic top-up may be offered only where the user has opted in. Manual top-up remains available for users who want spending control.

10 Course values and learner entitlements

Each course must have a recorded internal proposed credit value. The selected course value is automatically deducted from a learner's available allowance when the learner enrols. The allowance can be increased only by an approved extra-credit purchase or entitlement, and the maximum eligible course count still applies during the access period.

Internal proposed credits are a planning and entitlement measure. Under the APGI Course Development and Learning Credit Policy, one internal proposed learning credit represents 10 notional learning hours. This measure must not be presented as a recognised NQF credit, a qualification award or professional CPD unless the required recognition and learner-achievement conditions have been verified.

The platform must keep distinct records for internal proposed learning credits, course-creator credits, promotional credits and financial values. One must not be converted to another automatically.

10 1 Selecting credits or courses

The calculator provides a choice between an internal credit-allowance planning entry and selection of actual eligible courses. Selecting a course loads its exact edition, recorded scope, ownership and verified internal workload or proposed-credit value. Where several eligible courses are permitted, their recorded values are added automatically. The calculator must preserve the underlying unrounded workload record; it must not invent a credit rating from the course name, price, slides or video duration.

An individual-course purchase covers one learner and one named course. A named-course seat pack covers the approved number of places in one named course. Additional-course allowances must not be charged under either route. A learning wallet or platform-access subscription may include several eligible courses, subject to the approved course set, per-learner allowance, course-count cap and access term.

For a wallet or subscription bought before the actual courses are chosen, retain an unallocated prepaid learning balance until the approved course selections and allocation amounts can be determined. The terms must state the redemption values, expiry, treatment of unused allowance and applicable refund conditions. Do not distribute that balance as though it were already a sale of one identified course. Any special shared-course sale during development recovery requires an approved allocation schedule that identifies all recipients and the recovery beneficiary.

Learning-credit allowances are separate from formally recognised learner achievements, AI spending credits, development-funding credits and cash values. Course deployment must provide the required credit and workload record for that edition. Missing or unverified information may be used only in clearly marked planning estimates until the required record is completed.

11 Promotions and exceptions

The default model does not permit free learner enrolments. APGI may approve a promotion, sponsored cohort, pilot, scholarship or other exception where the approval records the course, scope, eligible learners, discount or waiver, funding source, start and end date, and the person responsible for the decision. A promotion does not change normal ownership, credit-recognition or client-access controls unless the approval states otherwise.

Any exception to a course scope, learner minimum, volume rule, recovery arrangement or hosting charge must be approved and retained with the commercial record. No commercial exception authorises the publication of unsupported formal credit claims or the disclosure of client-specific content.

12 Records approvals and change control

Before publication, the commercial record for each course must include the course owner, scope, eligible audience, recorded credit value, buying options, access period, course-count limit, price basis, volume rules, revenue allocation, fee treatment and ownership status. For APGI-developed courses it must also show the original development cost, recovery balance, recovery amount per sale and transfer conditions.

The course owner is responsible for the accuracy of its course record and for approval of any permitted sharing. APGI is responsible for maintaining the approved price schedule, platform-recovery assumptions and records of commission and recovery. The buyer is responsible for providing accurate learner and organisation information and for respecting eligibility restrictions.

Price changes apply prospectively. They must not silently alter an accepted learner or organisation commitment, an outstanding development-recovery record or a completed learner record. The policy owner must review this policy within 12 months of activation or sooner if the platform model, shared costs, payment treatment or applicable requirements materially change.

13 Activation and policy control

This document is for approval. It becomes effective only when the required APGI policy approvers record approval of the same exact version, the approval date, effective date and published policy reference. The approved platform pricing policy must be accessible to platform users from the policy library, course calculator and relevant purchase journey. Record the applicable policy version with each accepted commercial offer. Internal APGI and SRMS agreements and company-specific records retain their separate access restrictions. Activation of this policy does not itself activate a software feature, price, course, domain or learner entitlement.



Appendix A Commercial decision path

Use the following sequence when setting up an offer. The sequence ensures that access restrictions and learner entitlement are decided before price presentation.

Step | Decision | Required result

1 | Confirm the course record | Record the owner, scope, eligible audience, internal proposed credit value and whether APGI developed the course.

2 | Choose the buying route | Select individual course, named-course seat pack, learning wallet or platform access subscription.

3 | Confirm learner and organisation eligibility | Apply the public, industry-specific or client-specific rule before a course is displayed or sold.

4 | Set seats and access limits | Enter the exact learner count, access period, credit allowance and maximum eligible course count. Apply the group minimum where relevant.

5 | Calculate the buyer invoice | Apply course-content pricing, volume treatment, LMS platform recovery, card-fee treatment and tax treatment.

6 | Confirm allocation and recovery | Show course-owner, selling-platform and APGI allocations under section 8. For an APGI-developed course, show the approved temporary recovery amount, remaining balance and after-recovery split.

7 | Record approval and publish | Save the commercial record and obtain required approval before presenting the offer to learners or organisations.



Appendix B Required commercial record fields

The following information should be available to the calculator, checkout process and administrators. It supports a clear buyer invoice and an auditable revenue allocation.

Record group | Information required

Course identity | Course title, edition, owner, scope, eligibility rule, recorded internal proposed credit value and current learner status wording.

Access entitlement | Purchase option, selected seats, access period, learner credit allowance, maximum eligible course count and allowed course set.

Price basis | Course-content rate or cost-plus inputs, minimum content-price floor, volume adjustment, LMS recovery assumptions, card-fee treatment, tax treatment and currency.

Revenue allocation | Course owner, selling platform and APGI recipient identities and amounts. Use the applicable prescribed split. A third-party shared sale allocates 80 percent to the owner, 10 percent commission to the selling platform and 10 percent to APGI. Own-course and APGI-course resale arrangements follow section 8.

APGI development recovery | Original development cost, recovery balance, recovery amount per sale, sales history, date of full recovery and ownership-transfer confirmation.

Approvals and changes | Calculator and policy versions, approved price-schedule and cost-snapshot versions, course editions, required client or industry approval, exception record, effective date and retained change history.



Policy control record required for activation  exact policy version  authorised approver  approval decision and date  effective date  published policy reference

Appendix C Revision record

Version 1.1 Review draft dated 16 November 2026 corrects the third-party shared-course allocation to 80 percent course owner, 10 percent selling platform and 10 percent APGI. It also proposes controlled calculator access, selection of credits or courses, consistent platform-recovery assumptions, versioned commercial records and platform-wide access to the approved pricing policy. Version 1.0 and its records remain retained. No approval, price activation or payout is inferred by this revision.

Version 1.2 review addendum — 17 November 2026. New offers follow a conditions-first sequence: course editions, recorded scope and credits, permitted learners, buying method, quantity limits and access terms; then compare individual course, bulk named-course seats, learning wallet and prepaid platform access; then adjust the price per credit and any authorised external recipient allocations; finally review and approve a reusable exact version. Existing signed agreements, prices, policies and learner records retain their original basis.

The original progressive volume bands, commitment discounts and minimum content-price rules remain unchanged. Group prepaid discounts apply automatically. The individual-course shared-cost forecast is 20 concurrently active learners; group routes allocate the monthly pool across the quoted number of learner places. The full access term and variable once-per-enrolment costs are included. These denominators are assumptions, not proof of current sales, and can result in a higher per-learner group price at small quantities. The central platform-cost version is fixed within a price structure. Only supported new central cost versions may replace it prospectively. Defaults for public, industry and client-specific credit rates remain differentiated.

External recipient shares follow the section 8 defaults unless an exact new structure records a reason and the course owner’s authority for a negotiated alternative. Their percentages must reconcile to 100 percent of content income. The internal residual APGI/SRMS 50/50 distribution, cost reimbursement and recovery rules remain unchanged and private. Estimates are not realised profit and may not count a cost twice.

Johan Ras and Adriaan (Jorrie) Jordaan must separately approve the exact policy and each exact reusable price structure. Explicit policy activation and price-structure publication follow approval. A structure freezes the cost source, course editions, credit values, rates, allocation by course, payment-fee treatment, terms and quantity limits for all four options. An ordinary customer quote calculated strictly within the current published structure does not require fresh principal approval. An exception or a changed structure requires a new version. Client groups above 50 require the exception to be specifically recorded and approved.

Customer quotes expire after 24 hours if not accepted at checkout. A cart contains exact individual quotes in one currency and payment method, showing quantities, access terms, eligible course sets, content, platform recovery and processing provisions. Each item’s processing provision is retained on its frozen quote; the actual processor fee is reconciled once at the combined payment, never once per line. Any difference remains subject to reconciliation and does not authorise an additional unapproved charge. Buyer-paid fees require explicit approval and must be permitted for the relevant channel and jurisdiction before live use. Taxes and provider fees require verification before live launch.

Platform access is prepaid for a fixed term with no automatic renewal. Wallets and access packages record per-learner credit allowances, permitted editions, course caps, named assignment, expiry and immutable redemption history. Credit and content-money balances are updated atomically. Unspent funds remain unallocated. Expiry removes course access, not records or results; refunds and disputes block redemption and retain history. Bank invoice requests remain unpaid until separately verified; they do not fund allowances. Sandbox balances grant no live course access. Live payments remain disabled. No policy, commercial approval, entitlement, course publication, ownership transfer or payout is inferred by this draft.

Each company publishes pricing structures separately for each primary course. A new structure replaces only that company’s earlier structure for the same course. Other courses retain their own approved structures, and accepted checkout records retain their frozen prices.
